<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c0eecb1f808388998a0744a5f2cc46cdb4729a71` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ea0df331b130e3404574a6c6e797ea8d3bffa524` — the merge of head `c8366b960e5b35e99660382c43173d1314116685` into base `c0eecb1f808388998a0744a5f2cc46cdb4729a71`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea0df331b130e3404574a6c6e797ea8d3bffa524 && git checkout ea0df331b130e3404574a6c6e797ea8d3bffa524
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c0eecb1f808388998a0744a5f2cc46cdb4729a71 c8366b960e5b35e99660382c43173d1314116685 && git checkout -B drift-repro c0eecb1f808388998a0744a5f2cc46cdb4729a71 && git merge --no-ff c8366b960e5b35e99660382c43173d1314116685

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c0eecb1f808388998a0744a5f2cc46cdb4729a71
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c0eecb1f808388998a0744a5f2cc46cdb4729a71` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ca3ebc278c3ec6f82b8f2e19acb50724d4187e3c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/owd-sharing.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx, ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/en.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/zh.ts

PR #36579, card #36526. Inputs read: the card body and its 6 comments, the PR body and its 3 comments, the net diff against merge-base `ad50d611` (18 files, +471 / -47), and the check-runs on the head. The tests, the changeset body beyond section ②, and the generated files (`api-surface`, `export-origins`, three reference `.mdx`) are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set of `ObjectSchema` and `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`: unchanged. Both hunks only add `params` to an `addIssue` call that already existed; `controlledByParentMasterRefusal`'s predicate, paths and shapes are untouched. Right: `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- Public surface, widened, right: two new exports from `@objectstack/spec/data` (`CONTROLLED_BY_PARENT_MASTER_INVALID` const, `ControlledByParentMasterIssueParams` type; `data/index.ts:464` re-exports the module with `export *`), one new `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` member under `@objectstack/spec`, and a new `params` payload on an existing custom issue. Right: `Clause-②: yes` (ledger header, #16404: registering a code widens the face, door or no door).
- Raise sites: `controlledByParentMasterRefusal` has four callers at the head. Two turn the verdict into a zod issue and both now stamp `params` (`object.zod.ts:3728`, `stack.zod.ts:622`; `stack.zod.ts:604` is a guard that raises nothing). The other two raise no zod issue: `conversions/refused-shapes.ts:205` embeds `refusal.message` in the stored-row TODO and reports `refusal.shape` structurally, and `plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts:62` returns the message for a runtime write refusal. Neither is a parse issue and neither is a surface the Studio tab reads. So "both raise sites" is true.
- "One code, every shape": true. The function has six return arms and `ControlledByParentMasterShape` has six members; both raise sites copy `refusal.shape`, typed through `ControlledByParentMasterIssueParams`, so the two cannot drift.
- Message text: the three arms drop `ADR-0055 §1: ` and capitalise `Since`; the prescriptions are byte-unchanged. A search at the head for a test or code matcher on `ADR-0055 §1` or on the lower-case `since @objectstack/spec 18` finds none outside `object.test.ts`, which the diff updates. The remaining `ADR-0055 §1` hits are docblocks and comments. `refused-shapes.ts` appends the message after a full stop, so the new capital reads correctly there.
- Ledger row: placed alphabetically inside the `@objectstack/spec` entry, SCREAMING_SNAKE, `door: 'none'` on the `PLUGIN_UI_REQUIRED_KEY_MISSING` precedent (a code on a zod issue's `params.code`, no `status` of its own). The placement and the `door` / `status` reading follow the ledger header. The reachability sentence of the comment is finding S2.
- Check-runs on the head, as the gate verdicts: Lint and Repo Gates, every Lint shard, Type Check (source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core 1 to 8 of 10 and Test UI 1 to 5, 7 to 9, 11, 12, 15, 16 of 16 concluded success. PR-body guards failed on two earlier body revisions and concluded success on the latest two runs. Still `in_progress` at my last read (2026-11-23, about 00:45Z): Type Check · workspace, Test Core 9/10 and 10/10, Test UI 6, 10, 13 and 14 of 16. No completed run on the head is red. The record does not vouch for the unfinished ones.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/36526-cbp-refusal-business-wording.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, `@object-ui/i18n` patch, with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the changeset and the PR body.

Right. AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 sets the level from the metadata-protocol kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". Nothing a metadata author can write changes, so the two new exports and the new ledger code are a Clause-② widening that ships at patch. Check Changeset is green on the head.

Clause-②: yes

The changeset's last spec sentence ("a script that matched `ADR-0055 §1:` should match the code on `params.code` instead") holds for a reader of the zod issues and of `defineStack`'s `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` issues. It does not hold at the metadata save door; see S2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (L2 review at this head): this record.
- Open question 2 (code name): seat ruling 7088548226 accepts `CONTROLLED_BY_PARENT_MASTER_INVALID`. Nothing in the ledger rules speaks against it: it carries a domain prefix and is no synonym of a standard-catalog member.
- Open question 3 (exported params type): option A stands. It is type-only, and both raise sites annotate their literal with it, which is what keeps the two stamps identical.
- Dev deviation "patch on all three packages": correct, see ②.
- Dev deviation "generated files outside the file fence": forced by `check:generated`; lane seat's ACCEPT.
- Dev deviations on process (two pushes before overlap-check, gates run outside the verify lock, not re-merged with main `06c3e5ac`): no contract content; left to the lane seat.
- Out-of-scope finding folded into the PR in patch round 1 (the probe drops `readonly` / `system`): reviewed in ④; it leaves S1 open.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; it is a parse-issue payload, a ledger row and UI wording.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts` — the const, the params type and the three message edits hold against the card (a code a UI can localise from; no ADR number in product text) and against the first consumer, which reads `params.code` and `params.shape` off a client-side `ObjectSchema.safeParse`. On that path `params` is present by construction: there is no envelope between the parse and the reader, so the consumer is not a dead branch.

`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` — each stamps exactly what the jsdoc says, from the same refusal value that supplies the message.

`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` — the row is admissible; its comment carries S2.

`owd-sharing.ts`, `ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx`, `en.ts`, `zh.ts` — the shape-to-key map is typed on the spec's union (a seventh shape fails type-check), `refusalShape` requires the spec's code and an own-property shape, the fallback with no code or an unknown shape is the spec message, and en and zh each carry the same eight keys (six shapes, the field quote, the separator). Field naming uses the label when it is a non-empty string, else the key. The flag copy takes `readonly` and `system` only when boolean and only on a `master_detail`, which is what the spec's `=== true` reading needs.

S1 (should-fix) — `refusalFields` resolves the `master-not-writable` field on the RAW probe, while the spec judged the PARSED one, and the two disagree on an omitted `required`. Take a `controlled_by_parent` object whose one `master_detail` writes no `required` and carries `readonly: true` (or `system: true`). `cbpMasterRefusal` builds the probe without `required`; `ObjectSchema` defaults it to `false`, reads the field as the optional master and refuses it with shape `master-not-writable` (module header of `controlled-by-parent-master.ts`: through a raw parse an omitted `required` is the optional master). `refusalFields` then calls `controlledByParentMasterOf(probe)` on the unparsed map, where `required` is `undefined`, so it names no master and returns no field. `cbpRefusalText` substitutes an empty string for `{field}`, and the tab prints "... through , but that field is read-only or a system field ... Make  editable ..." in en and the same gap in zh. The shape is reachable on any object that arrives already `controlled_by_parent` (authored in code or installed from a package), and on a master added after the sharing model was picked, since `requireCbpMasterDetails` runs only on the pick. The tests cover a flagged master with `required: true` and with `required: false` only. The fix is local to `refusalFields`: name the single required `master_detail`, else the only `master_detail`. The docblock sentence "read off the same probe the spec judged" should then say which reading it uses.

S2 (should-fix) — the reachability reading in two hits files says the code rides the door's envelope, and at the metadata save door it does not. The ledger comment reads "It rides the envelope of whichever door parses the object", and the const's jsdoc reads "raised at authoring and at the save door's parse, and rides that door's own envelope". The save door maps its issues through `zodIssuesToMetadataIssues` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-metadata-issues.ts`), whose entry is `{ path, message, code }` with `code` being zod's own issue code. A refused object save therefore answers `422 INVALID_METADATA` with `issues[]` entries of `code: 'custom'` and no `params`; `CONTROLLED_BY_PARENT_MASTER_INVALID` is not on that wire. The precedent row is not in the same position: `PLUGIN_UI_REQUIRED_KEY_MISSING` is also written at the head of the issue `message`, so it survives a flattening envelope, and this code is deliberately kept out of the message. The code is observable on the zod issue itself (any `safeParse`, which is the Studio tab's path) and on `defineStack`'s `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` refusal, whose `issues` are the raw zod issues. The ledger header makes the row comment the place the reachability reading lives, so the sentence is part of the published face. Correct both sentences, and the changeset's `params.code` advice with them, to name where the code is and is not carried. Carrying `params` through the save door envelope would be a wire change and belongs on its own card.

N1 (nit) — `cbpMasterRefusal` still picks the first custom issue at `sharingModel` or `fields` by position. Now that the refusal carries a code, preferring the issue whose `params.code` matches would keep another refinement at those paths from taking the slot. No such issue arises on the reduced probe today.

N2 (nit) — the en row for `required-lookup-only` is plural ("only the required lookup fields {fields}") and reads oddly with one lookup; zh has no number agreement and is fine.

S1 and S2 are open on this head. Neither changes which objects are refused or what the spec publishes as code and shape, so the verdict below stands on the contract; the head still owes a delta review of the two fixes before it lands.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c8366b960e5b35e99660382c43173d1314116685`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/owd-sharing.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx, ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/en.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/zh.ts

Delta round 1 on PR #36579, card #36526. The previous at-tier record is PR comment 7088626814 at head `ca3ebc27` (PASS, with S1 and S2 open, N1 and N2 noted). Inputs read: the card body and its 7 comments, the PR body and its 5 comments, the net diff against merge-base `ad50d611` (18 files, +530 / -50), the rework alone `ca3ebc27..c8366b96` (one commit, 9 files, +74 / -18), and the check-runs on the head. The tests, the generated files and the changeset body beyond section ② are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- Rework extent, spec half: comments only. `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` changes lines of the `//` comment above the row; `controlled-by-parent-master.ts` changes lines of the const's JSDoc. `object.zod.ts` and `stack.zod.ts` are byte-identical between the two heads. No code, no export, no ledger member and no message text moved, so every derived judgment of record 7088626814 on the accept-set (unchanged), the public surface (two exports from `@objectstack/spec/data`, one ledger member, `params` on an existing custom issue) and the raise sites (two, both stamping) stands on this head as written there.
- Generated files: not touched by the rework, and rightly. The three reference `.mdx` pages and the two `data.json` baselines carry the bare code name only, not the row comment or the JSDoc sentence, so a comment edit regenerates nothing.
- Rework extent, ui half: `refusalFields` (the `master-not-writable` arm), the issue selection in `cbpMasterRefusal`, the key choice in `cbpRefusalText`, one new language-pack key in en and zh, and two test files. Which objects the tab reports as refused is unchanged: the verdict is still `ObjectSchema.safeParse` on the same probe.
- Main not merged in this hop: `git merge-base origin/main` is `ad50d611` for both `ca3ebc27` and `c8366b96`.
- Check-runs on the head (51 listed, read about 01:16Z on 2026-11-23). Concluded success: Type Check · source gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset (both runs), PR-body guards (both runs), Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, filter, Auto Label. Still `in_progress`: Test Core 1 to 10 of 10, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build Docs, Live E2E UI, every Lint shard (CI, release and engine gates; ESLint; repo and tooling gates; docs and code guards; PM dispatch-gates; the three scoped shards), Type Check · workspace, · consumer gates and · debt ledger. The Test UI shards, Type Check UI and Lint UI were not yet listed. No completed run on the head is red. This record does not vouch for the unfinished or unlisted ones; the rework changes ui source, so Test UI and Type Check UI are the runs that answer for it.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/36526-cbp-refusal-business-wording.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, `@object-ui/i18n` patch, with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in the changeset and in the PR body. Unchanged by the rework and still right: `Metadata-protocol: none` sets `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3), and the widening (two exports, one ledger code, now nine `cbpRefusal*` language-pack keys per locale) ships at that level. Check Changeset is green on the head.

Clause-②: yes

The rework rewrote the one changeset sentence S2 named. It now tells a script to match `params.code` on the zod issue where it can see the issue (an `ObjectSchema` / `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` `safeParse`, or the `issues` of `defineStack`'s `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` refusal) and says the save door's `422 INVALID_METADATA` keeps `path`, `message` and zod's issue code only. That is what the head does; see S2 below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question of dev report 7088965055 (delta review of S1 and S2 at this head): this record.
- Dev deviation "not merged with origin/main": confirmed above; no contract content, left to the lane seat.
- Dev deviation "N1 has no dedicated test": accepted. On the reduced probe no second custom issue arises at `sharingModel` or `fields`, so no fixture can tell the two selections apart, and the change cannot alter today's result.
- Out-of-scope finding of dev report 7088965055 (class b: the save door's `issues[]` drops `params`, so a client of that door cannot read the registered code): escalated to the lane seat. The brief speaks of a separate card; neither the card thread nor the PR body names one. The PR body says only that carrying `params` through that envelope "would be a wire change and is not made here". The finding should be filed as its own card before this one closes, so the published sentence "NOT on the metadata save door" has an owner. It is not a defect of this diff: the three sentences state the gap truthfully.
- Earlier flags (code name ruling 7088548226, the exported params type, patch level, generated files outside the fence): answered in record 7088626814; nothing in the rework reopens them.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The rework adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed — `refusalFields` now names the master of a `master-not-writable` refusal as the parse reads it. The arm takes the `master_detail` entries whose probe `required` is `true`; with exactly one it returns that one, otherwise it returns the only `master_detail`, otherwise nothing. Against `controlledByParentMasterOf` on the PARSED map (module header and the function's own docblock: one `required: true` master is the master whatever stands beside it; with none, the only `master_detail`, whose omitted `required` has defaulted to `false`, is the optional master) the two agree on every input that can carry this shape, because the probe copies `required` only when it is a boolean and the parse default only ever writes `false`, so "probe `required === true`" and "parsed `required === true`" select the same fields. Cases tried by reading:
  - two `master_detail`, one `required: true` and flagged: the spec's master is the required one; the arm returns it.
  - two `master_detail`, one `required: true` unflagged, the other flagged: the spec refuses nothing (the flag is judged on the one master only); no refusal reaches the arm.
  - two `master_detail`, none required: shape `several-masters`, a different arm.
  - two `required: true`: shape `several-required-masters`, a different arm.
  - one `master_detail`, `required: false` written, `readonly: true`: named.
  - one `master_detail`, `required` omitted, `system: true`: named (this is the case S1 reported empty).
  - one `master_detail`, `required: 'true'` as a string, flagged: the probe drops the non-boolean, the parse reads the optional master, the arm names the field.
  The empty return is now unreachable under this shape: the spec raises `master-not-writable` only when it resolved a master, which means exactly one required `master_detail`, or none required and exactly one `master_detail`. `cbpRefusalText` therefore always has `names[0]`, and the en and zh rows no longer print a gap. The docblock now says which reading it uses and why the raw probe would name no master; each sentence is true of the spec module at the head. The new cases (omitted `required` with `readonly`, with `system`; the panel row in en and zh) pin it, and the dev's ablation of the only-`master_detail` arm is reported as failing exactly those two.

S2: closed — the three sentences now say where the code is and is not carried, and each holds at the head.
  - "on the zod issue itself (any `safeParse`, the Studio tab's path)": `object.zod.ts:3734` and the extension gate at `stack.zod.ts:622` pass `params` to `ctx.addIssue`, and `cbpMasterRefusal` reads `issue.params` straight off `ObjectSchema.safeParse` with no envelope between.
